z_{P,a}(x)=|\omega_a(x)|\sigma_a(x),
\qquad
\Phi(z)=\min_{\substack{u_a\geq\varepsilon\\\sum_a u_a=1}}
\sum_a\frac{z_a^2}{u_a},
\]
one has
\[
V^*(P)=\operatorname{Var}_P\{h_P(X_t)\}+E_P\Phi\{z_P(X_t)\}.
\tag{58}
\]
Thus any centered Bayes converse is exactly a lower bound on the posterior variance in (57) after subtracting the prior mean of the two terms in (58) divided by \(n\).

defs.def:design-class: \(\mathfrak D_{n,\varepsilon}:=\{D=(q_t^D)_{t=1}^n: q_t^D\text{ is a law-independent assignment kernel satisfying kernel measurability, normalization, and positivity}\}\). Each kernel is a function only of \(a\), the current covariate \(x\), and the realized past history \(h\in\mathcal H_{t-1}\).
defs.def:induced-experiment: For \(D\in\mathfrak D_{n,\varepsilon}\) and \(P\in\mathcal P(s,r)\), draw \(U_1,\ldots,U_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), reveal the baseline covariates allowed by the fixed information order in \(H_0\), and recursively draw \(A_t\mid(X_t,H_{t-1})\sim q_t^D(\cdot\mid X_t,H_{t-1})\), set \(Y_t:=Y_t(A_t)\), and append \(O_t=(X_t,A_t,Y_t)\) to the history. This defines \(\mathbb P_n^{D,P}\), \(\mathcal F_t^{D,P}:=\sigma(H_t)\), and \(e_{t,a}^{D,P}:=\mathbb P_n^{D,P}(A_t=a\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{D,P},X_t)=q_t^D(a\mid X_t,H_{t-1})\) almost surely.
defs.def:model-class: \(\mathcal P(s,r):=\{P: P\text{ is a law of }U_t\text{ satisfying the bounded-density, Gaussian-outcome, mean-Hölder, mean-bound, variance-Hölder, and variance-range conditions}\}\). The radii and bounds are fixed independently of \(n\).
defs.def:oracle-benchmark: For \(e_a(x)\ge\varepsilon\) and \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}e_a(x)=1\), define \[V(e;P):=\operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\omega_a(X_t)\mu_a(X_t)\right)+E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{m_a(X_t)}{e_a(X_t)}\right],\qquad V^*(P):=\inf_e V(e;P).\]

assumptions.ass:kernel-positivity: \(q_t^D(a\mid x,h)\ge\varepsilon\) for every \(t\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), \(x\in[0,1]^d\), and \(h\in\mathcal H_{t-1}\).
assumptions.ass:kernel-measurability: For every \(t\), \(q_t^D(a\mid x,h)\) is jointly measurable in \(a\), \(x\), and \(h\in\mathcal H_{t-1}\).
assumptions.ass:kernel-normalization: \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}q_t^D(a\mid x,h)=1\) for every \(t\), \(x\in[0,1]^d\), and \(h\in\mathcal H_{t-1}\).
